mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.5% within the last month signals a tightening monetary policy, which typically leads to a decrease in S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as borrowing costs rise and economic activity slows.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the correlation between FEDFUNDS increases and negative SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the unemployment rate by more than 0.5% within the last month indicates a weakening labor market, which historically correlates with negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as consumer spending and business investment decline.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the correlation between UNRATE increases and negative SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A significant drop in real GDP by more than 1% over the last quarter signals a contraction in economic activity, which typically results in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as corporate earnings and economic outlook worsen.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the correlation between GDPC1 decreases and negative SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production by more than 2% over the last month signals a strengthening supply side, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as market sentiment improves.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 5-day returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or the correlation between INDPRO increases and positive SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained low inflation environment, indicated by CPIAUCSL remaining below 200 for three consecutive months, signals a stable economic environment, which typically results in positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as investor confidence increases.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or the correlation between low CPIAUCSL and positive SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in housing starts by more than 5% over the last two months signals a weakening demand in the housing market, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as a broader economic slowdown is anticipated.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the correlation between HOUST decreases and negative SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: An interaction between a rising unemployment rate and a decrease in nonfarm payrolls indicates a weakening labor market, which typically results in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as consumer spending and business investment decline.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE increases > 0.3% and PAYEMS decreases > 0.5% in 1 month
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the joint effect of UNRATE and PAYEMS changes on negative SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) by more than 1% over the last three months signals a strengthening consumer demand, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as corporate earnings and economic outlook improve.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in > 40% of instances despite the positive signal, or the correlation between RSAFS increases and positive SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).
